policy_changes.summary: decision-review --apply changes a book's knobs only when track_statistics.json (at most 4 days old, same benchmark) gives that book a positive or negative verdict, i.e. a 90% interval on annualised active return that excludes zero. Missing, stale, thin or noise-level statistics keep the review a proposal; --force does not bypass it. Replaces the legacy rule (thick history + excess beyond +/-2% on the knob epoch), which tuned on noise.
policy_changes.history_note: Knob epochs started before effective_at were applied under the legacy threshold rule; do not read their returns as evidence for the knobs they set. History is not rewritten. The primary (ai_judgment_fair) and control (buy_tier_level) never had a legacy apply, so the primary-vs-control comparison is unaffected. Review rows carry apply_policy from this date. Audit counts come from decision_review_history.json, which keeps the last 52 reviews, so they are lower bounds for older books.

policy_changes.summary: B3 evidentiary demotion: ai_judgment_fair (3-name sleeve) is no longer adoption / filter-skill truth. Judgment evidence moves to N210 fixed-stake fair-cost episode %; portfolio continuity via matched-30 fund twin pair. Do not enlarge live max_positions/sector_cap mid-flight. Do not back-label prior 3-name NAV as evidence for the new epoch. F8: trailing primary-vs-control gap never alone applies knobs or fills.
policy_changes.history_note: Marks and NAV on ai_judgment_fair before and after effective_at remain continuity / observe history. They are underpowered and confounded (sleeve N=3 vs control ~55) and must not be read as filter skill or as evidence for matched-30 / N210 skill. assessment_model.primary_track may still name ai_judgment_fair for product continuity until volume gates; policy_changes.evidentiary_demotion_ai_judgment_fair_v1 is the demotion stamp.
